query: What are the best practices for implementing authentication in microservices?

results.content: Authentication in microservices requires careful consideration of token propagation. Use JWT tokens with short expiration times (15 minutes) for access tokens and longer-lived refresh tokens (7 days). Implement token validation at the API gateway level to reduce redundant validation across services.

Service-to-service authentication should use mTLS (mutual TLS) for internal communication. This ensures that each service can verify the identity of other services it communicates with. Certificate rotation should be automated using tools like cert-manager or Vault.

Centralized authentication through an identity provider (IdP) like OAuth2/OIDC is recommended. This allows for single sign-on (SSO) across all microservices and centralized user management. Popular choices include Keycloak, Auth0, and AWS Cognito.

Implement rate limiting and throttling at the authentication endpoints to prevent brute force attacks. Use exponential backoff for failed login attempts and implement CAPTCHA after 3 failed attempts. Log all authentication events for security auditing.

Store sensitive credentials and API keys in a secrets management system like HashiCorp Vault or AWS Secrets Manager. Never hardcode credentials in application code or configuration files. Use environment variables injected at runtime.

results.description: Centralize authentication at API gateway, validate tokens once
results.implementation: Use Kong, Traefik, or AWS API Gateway with JWT validation plugin

results.description: Use service mesh to handle service-to-service authentication via mTLS
results.implementation: Deploy Istio or Linkerd with automatic mTLS
results.example_code:
# Istio mTLS config
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: PeerAuthentication
metadata:
  name: default
spec:
  mtls:
    mode: STRICT

results.description: Use OAuth2 token exchange for secure service-to-service calls
results.implementation: Implement RFC 8693 token exchange with identity provider

results.description: Deploy authentication proxy as sidecar to each service
results.implementation: Use Envoy or Ambassador as authentication sidecar
results.example_code:
// Envoy JWT filter
filters:
- name: envoy.filters.http.jwt_authn
  typed_config:
    providers:
      auth_provider:
        issuer: https://auth.example.com
        remote_jwks:
          http_uri:
            uri: https://auth.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json

results.description: Use Redis or similar for shared session storage across services
results.implementation: Configure Redis cluster with session middleware
